note: Recast from Hill 1922; the original is in English (New and rare Australian termites, with notes on their biology, Proc. Linn. Soc. N.S.W.). The original uses the hyphen as a decimal point as well, which has been changed to a decimal point; the measurements of the small soldier are given in the original after the figure captions, outside the OCR coverage of this section, and are not recorded. Figures 41—50 (alate head, antennal basal segment, mandibles, base of the hindwing; large soldier head, pronotum, hind leg, antennal basal segment; small soldier head, antennal basal segment) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldiers dimorphic, large and small: in the large soldier the head is subsquare, broadly rounded posteriorly, the sides slightly divergent to the posterior margin of the antennal sockets and then narrowed to the mandibular base, the postclypeus with a deep median groove running from the fontanelle to the tip of the labrum; mandibles stout, the left with 2 apical teeth, the right with 1; antenna 17—18-segmented; pronotum wider than the head, flattened, with upturned margins, convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly. In the small soldier the head is small, widest behind the antennal sockets, narrower posteriorly, the antenna 16-segmented, segment 4 the shortest.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body above ochraceous tawny, beneath yellow ochre; wings hyaline, the anterior margin yellow ochre. Head small, rounded posteriorly and laterally, flattened dorsoventrally, concave in the middle of the dorsum, slightly rugose around the fontanelle, sparsely hairy. Labrum slightly convex, narrow at the base, widening laterally to the width of the postclypeus, with a few red setae. Anteclypeus membranous, two-thirds as long as the postclypeus, leaf-like in the middle. Postclypeus convex, divided in the middle by an iron-coloured suture, slightly wider than long, the posterior margin slightly arcuate, the anterior margin truncate, with a few red setae. Compound eyes very large and prominent, subcircular (0.399×0.446 mm). Ocelli large, broadly oval, about one-third of their long diameter from the compound eyes. Fontanelle large, circular. Mandibles: the left with 4 pointed teeth, the right with 2, the latter separated by a small horn-shaped tooth. Antenna 20-segmented: segment 1 short, square, almost wider than long; segment 2 square, half as long as segment 1; segment 3 slightly longer and wider than segment 2, top-shaped; segments 4 and 5 subequal in length, shorter and narrower than segment 3, slightly top-shaped; segments 6 and 7 subequal in length, similar to segments 4 and 5 but larger; segments 7—20 moniliform. Pronotum narrower than the head, the anterior margin truncate and slightly upturned, the sides rounded, the posterior margin bilobed, the outer margin with moderately long red setae. Wing rudiments large, moderately hairy, the anterior pair 1.03 long, twice the posterior pair. Legs moderately short and slender, the femora slightly stout, with scattered red setae. Tibial spurs 3:3:2, long and slender. Abdomen short and broad, rounded at the apex, the posterior halves of the tergites and sternites very sparsely hairy, the pleurites densely hairy. Cerci short and stout. Styli present in the male only. Measurements (mm): length with wings 11.0—11.5; length without wings 7.0; head length (base to clypeal base) 1.03; head width (including compound eyes) 1.41; head depth 0.80; antenna (20 segments) length 2.50; pronotum length 0.75, width 1.18; forewing length 9.00, width 2.85; hindwing length 8.75, width 3.00; hind tibia 1.05; abdominal width 1.64.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: body above yellow ochre, the antennae, legs and underside slightly paler, postclypeus hazel, mandibles iron-coloured. Head large, square, broadly rounded posteriorly, the sides slightly divergent to the posterior margin of the antennal sockets and then narrowed to the mandibular base, with sparse stout red setae. Labrum large, about twice as long as the postclypeus, covering the apical teeth of the mandibles, slightly swollen laterally, deeply excised anteriorly. Postclypeus large, with a deep median groove running from the fontanelle to the tip of the labrum. Fontanelle large. Mandibles very stout, the left with 2 apical teeth, the right with 1. Antenna 17 or 18 segments, segment 3 the shortest but only slightly shorter than segments 4 and 5, segments 5—17 moniliform, segment 18 small, broadly oval. Pronotum wider than the head, flattened, with upturned margins, the anterior margin convex, the sides inclined towards the concave posterior margin, with sparse short stout red setae. Mesonotum and metanotum wider than the pronotum, similarly hairy. Legs rather slender. Tibial spurs 3:2:2. Abdomen broad and flat, widest in the middle, broad at the base, bluntly rounded at the apex, the segments sparsely hairy. Cerci large, broad at the base, conical at the apex. Styli present. Measurements (mm): total length 5.5; thorax and abdomen length 3.10; head length (base to labral tip) 2.20, width 1.55, depth 0.89; antennal length 1.92; mandible length 1.03; pronotum length 0.66, width 1.18; hind tibia 1.27; abdominal width 1.31. Small soldier: body yellow ochre, postclypeus ochraceous tawny, mandibles pale iron-coloured. Head small, widest behind the antennal sockets, narrower posteriorly, the posterior margin broadly rounded, hairy as in the large soldier. Labrum slender and long, sparsely hairy at the apex. Postclypeus broad, the anterior margin nearly truncate. Antenna 16-segmented, segment 4 the shortest, segments 5—13 moniliform, segments 14 and 15 top-shaped, segment 16 small, broadly oval. Mandibles large, the dentition as in the large soldier. Pronotum shaped as in the large soldier.
